reason: Light-sensitive cells and relay cells appear to form the retina's sensing and signaling network.
expectation: They will form a retina that detects light and passes signals onward.

effect: The retinas connect light-sensitive cells to nerve fibers, so they can now be fitted into the eyes.
reaction: The link from sensing light to passing signals onward is clear.
reason: The eye walls appear to provide the structure that holds the retinas.
expectation: The retinas will fit inside the eye walls.

effect: The retinas are installed in eye cups, which have three named slots for front fittings.
reaction: The marked slots make the next steps clear.
reason: The corneas are transparent curved fronts, so they fit the clear fronts slot.
expectation: The corneas will fit into the clear fronts slot.

effect: The corneas are fitted, leaving the focusing lenses and light controls to add.
reason: The lenses match the focusing lenses slot.
expectation: The lenses will fit into the eye cups.

effect: The lenses are fitted, leaving the light controls slot open.
reason: The irises surround the pupils and match the light controls slot.
expectation: The irises will fit into the eye cups.

effect: All three front fittings are in place, and the result explains how they focus and control incoming light.
reaction: The ray description makes the parts' roles clearer.
reason: The visual pathways should connect the completed eye cups to the brain.
expectation: The visual pathways will connect to the eyes so retinal signals can travel toward the brain.

effect: The eyes now have pathways carrying retinal signals toward brain relays; they still need movement and connection to the body.
reaction: The distinction between incoming light and outgoing nerve signals is clear.
reason: The eye-moving muscles and nerves should equip the eyes to move, as the goal requires.
expectation: The muscles and nerves will attach to the eyes and enable movement.

effect: The eyes connected to the body automatically; the eye-moving muscles and nerves still need to be added.
reaction: I expected the muscles to attach first, so the required order was surprising.
reason: The remaining muscles and nerves appear to provide the eye movement required by the goal.
expectation: The muscles and nerves will connect to the body's eyes and enable them to move.

effect: The eye-moving muscles and nerves completed the connected eyes and the chapter’s goal.
reaction: The final image of the body turning its eyes toward a face gives the assembled parts a clear purpose.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the visual pathways was most worthwhile: the comparison between incoming light and outgoing nerve signals clarified what the eyes send to the brain.

leastWorthwhile.text: The three successive front fittings were clear but a little repetitive. Their combined ray description made their roles more meaningful afterward.

surprise.text: I expected to attach the eye-moving muscles before connecting the eyes to the body. The compatibility feedback instead connected the body automatically.

arbitrary.text: The required order for adding the eye muscles felt somewhat arbitrary; the initial descriptions did not explain why they had to follow the body connection.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter to see how another body system connects to the whole. The signal-versus-light distinction was interesting, though the straightforward fittings were less engaging.
